html:
The Yakama are a Sahaptin-speaking people of the Columbia Plateau in central Washington, from the Yakima River valley east of the Cascades. The map uses the older spelling Yakima.

They lived by the salmon runs of the Columbia and its tributaries, and by gathering roots and berries in the uplands. They traded at the great fishing places on the Columbia with the Tenino, Umatilla, Palouse and others, and kept large horse herds after the 1700s.

In 1855 fourteen tribes and bands signed a treaty that created the Yakama Nation and its reservation, giving up most of their land. Gold seekers soon crossed the land, and the Yakima War of 1855 to 1858, led by the chief Kamiakin, ended in defeat. The Yakama Nation, with its reservation south of the city of Yakima, still holds treaty fishing rights. The map also shows them as Yakama.
